title: Chepstow named Wales' most haunted racecourse as Halloween approaches
excerpt: Chepstow has been named Wales' most haunted racecourse according to new data.
content:
Chepstow Racecourse is the most haunted in Wales according to new data (Image: Chepstow Racecourse)

This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald.

Chepstow has been named Wales' most haunted racecourse.

With a score of 3.54 out of 10, Chepstow came 43rd in a list of 60 UK racecourses ranked by AskGamblers on cemetery distance, age, and paranormal reports.

The ranking comes in the year of Chepstow's centenary, with the course opening in 1926.

The track is 0.22 miles from the nearest burial ground.

Wales' other courses also appeared in the list: Bangor-on-Dee was placed 45th, and Ffos Las, the youngest course in the ranking (opened in 2009), was ranked 55th.

Chester topped the UK ranking with a score of 8.27.

The highest-ranked course in Scotland is Kelso (15th, 4.71), and in Northern Ireland, Down Royal (joint 8th, 5.19).

Huntingdon was the least haunted course in the ranking (1.55).

The ranking was based on three factors: distance to the nearest cemetery, how long racing has been recorded there, and the number of paranormal reports in its town.
